chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That a man from Khas'am came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'Which of the deeds is the most hated to Allah, Mighty and Majestic?' He said, 'The association (Shirk) with Allah.' He said, 'Then what?' He said, 'Cutting off the relationship.' He said, 'Then what?' He said, 'Enjoining the evil and forbidding the good.'

key_terms.الشِّرْكُ: Association of partners with God; polytheism
key_terms.الْأَمْرُ بِالْمُنْكَرِ: Enjoining or commanding what is evil/wrong
key_terms.قَطِيعَةُ الرَّحِمِ: Cutting off kinship ties or family relations

ai.seo_question: What are the three most hated deeds to Allah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the hierarchy of major sins, positioning Shirk as the root of disbelief, followed by the social rupture of cutting kinship ties, and finally the communal failure of enjoining evil while forbidding good. In Shia scholarship, this triad illustrates how theological deviation leads to social fragmentation and moral decay, serving as the foundational 'corner-stones' of disbelief. The sequence emphasizes that while Shirk is the primary offense against God, the neglect of social and moral duties constitutes the practical manifestation of that spiritual decline.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Talha Bin Zayd, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>,

‘A man from Khas’am came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and he said, ‘Which of the deeds is the most Hated one to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The association (Shirk) with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. He said, ‘Then what?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Cutting off the relationship’. He said, ‘Then what?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Enjoining of the evil and forbidding from the good’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Talhah ibn Zayd from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Once a man from Khath’am (a tribe) came to the Holy Prophet and asked, ‘Which of the acts is more resented in the sight of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy?’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Considering things as partners of Allah.’ The man asked, then what is more resented?’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Disregard of maintaining good relations with relatives.’ The man asked, ‘Then what is more resented?’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Commanding others to commit unlawful acts and prohibiting them to perform obligatory ones.’”
